thesis: The speaker argues that the private credit market froze initially because no underwriting models could predict pandemic outcomes, leading investors to sell uncertainty rather than buy distressed assets. He explains that short-duration assets required immediate action as maturities approached, while longer-duration assets allowed for deferral, and notes that subprime consumer loans have not yet seen significant default spikes despite economic stress.
